clue.text: Badly affected by dismissal, so retire

parts.note: to be hit by something is to be badly affected by it
getting the sack is being dismissed from a job

explanation.surface: A sacked worker, hurt by losing the job, decides to give up and step away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retire' looks like leaving work, matching the dismissal story, but here it means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for going to bed, which is one sense of retiring for the night.

clue.text: In which a spindle is part of a lock

indicators.note: In says the letters sit inside the run of words which a spindle

explanation.surface: Describing a lock mechanism with a spindle inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In which' reads as a relative phrase, but 'In' is the signal and the letters straddle whicH A SPindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged metal plate that fits over a staple and is secured with a padlock, a fastening component.

clue.text: Start to talk to stern president

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the word talk

parts.note: aft is the stern, rear part, of a ship

explanation.surface: Begin addressing a severe head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' looks like an adjective describing the president, but it is the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: William Howard Taft was the 27th US President.

clue.text: Writ has lumped Lincoln in with another Oxford college

indicators.note: lumped ... in means one word is thrown inside another
in shows Lincoln's first name goes inside has

parts.note: taken as written
Abe Lincoln, the US president; Lincoln is also an Oxford college
Corpus Christi is an Oxford college

explanation.surface: A document groups Lincoln College with another Oxford college.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln is indeed an Oxford college, hence 'another', but here it means Abraham Lincoln, the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal order requiring a detained person be brought before a court.

clue.text: Lorna's turned up sporting no English headgear

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top
sporting no means having none of the following letter

parts.note: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R D Blackmore's novel, so Lorna's gives her surname with s

explanation.surface: Lorna arrives wearing nothing English on her head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting no' drops the E from DOONES, giving DOONS, and 'turned up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairnet or band worn over the hair or neck, a kind of headwear.

clue.text: This can lessen mess

indicators.note: mess says the letters of can lessen are jumbled up

explanation.surface: Something is praised as a way of reducing untidiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like the object of 'lessen' but it is the signal for rearranging CAN LESSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiness and freedom from dirt reduce disorder, so the whole clue describes the quality.

clue.text: Sleeping principally beside cat — that's bad for the chest

indicators.note: principally means taking the first, chief letter of the word sleeping

parts.note: MOG is British slang for a cat, short for moggy

explanation.surface: A cat dozes by the sleeper, and someone warns that this is harmful for the lungs.
explanation.walkthrough: MOG (or moggy) is British informal for an ordinary cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Polluted fog over a city irritates the lungs and airways, so it is harmful to breathing.

clue.text: Remarkably good, a romantic sort of marriage

indicators.note: remarkably suggests the letters are rearranged in a striking new way

explanation.surface: An unusually fine, romantic kind of wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A union between a royal and a lower-ranked partner where the spouse gets no title or inheritance.

clue.text: Veterans go to review memorial

indicators.note: to review here is to re-view, reordering the letters of veterans go

explanation.surface: Old soldiers go to inspect a war monument.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone marks and commemorates a dead person, so it is a memorial.

clue.text: Criminal, not so bright, gets a month inside

indicators.note: inside places the month phrase within the word for less bright

parts.note: slower means less quick-witted, not so bright
Feb is the short form of February

explanation.surface: A dim-witted crook is sent down for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' suggests a prison term, which suits the criminal; it is only the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A safeblower is a thief who cracks safes with explosives, so a kind of criminal.

clue.text: Girl I found at Sandhurst

parts.note: Sandhurst is home of the Royal Military Academy, RMA, the British army officer school

explanation.surface: Someone says they met a young woman at the military academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Irma is a female first name, and crosswords freely clue first names by sex.

clue.text: The company of princes, perhaps, all top scientists

definitions.meaning: princes are members of the royal family, so their company is a regal gathering
the UK's national academy of sciences, whose fellows are leading scientists

explanation.surface: A gathering of princes, or of the most eminent scientists.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a royal gathering, and the name of Britain's academy of leading scientists.

clue.text: Servant, one sent to time the Titanic's trip

parts.note: a maid is a female servant
an envoy is someone sent on a mission
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A servant is dispatched to clock how long the great liner's crossing takes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titanic sank on its first ever sailing, the inaugural crossing of a new ship.

clue.text: A courtly lack of conviction may be his failing

definitions.text: A courtly lack of conviction may be his failing

parts.words: A courtly lack of conviction may be his failing
parts.note: courtly means in a court of law, and lack of conviction is an acquittal, the failure of the lawyer bringing the case

explanation.surface: A gallant suitor whose weakness is half-heartedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courtly' and 'conviction' suggest manners and belief; read legally, they mean a trial and a guilty verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: The lawyer who brings a criminal case fails when the court does not convict.

clue.text: One in bed wanting to sleep bore being cuddled by lad

indicators.note: being cuddled by means held inside the word for a boy

parts.note: a lad, a boy, is a son
a nap is a short sleep
a drag is something tedious, a bore

explanation.surface: A sleepy, dull bedfellow is hugged by a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a flower bed, not a place to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden flower, so one plant found in a flower bed.

clue.text: Call round for four evenings of music

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
a cycle is a round, a repeating series

explanation.surface: Someone phones round to arrange four nights of concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's Der Ring des Nibelungen is four operas, traditionally staged on four evenings.

clue.text: Thane protected by shield combining distinct styles

indicators.note: protected by means the thane sits inside the word for a shield

parts.note: cover is protection, a shield
Ross is a Scottish thane in Shakespeare's Macbeth

explanation.surface: A Scottish lord behind a shield blends different styles.
explanation.walkthrough: A thane is a Scottish lord; Ross is one of Macbeth's thanes.
explanation.definitionFit: A work or style that mixes genres, such as music fusing two traditions.

clue.text: Stop on board to give a description of the ocean

parts.note: the ocean may well be described as vast, huge

explanation.surface: An order to halt aboard a ship is given, alongside a portrait of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor's command meaning stop or cease, used aboard ship.

clue.text: Policeman's pressure breaks man in court

indicators.note: breaks means the pressure letter breaks into the word for a litigant

parts.note: a suer is someone bringing a lawsuit in court
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A police officer's pressure cracks a man on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: A super is short for superintendent, a senior British police rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for superintendent, a senior British police officer rank.

clue.text: Died before committee meeting — there's a thing!

parts.note: OB is short for Latin obiit, he or she died, seen on gravestones
a committee sits in session

explanation.surface: Someone died just before a committee met, prompting an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a thing about something is an informal way of saying you are fixated on it.

clue.text: Happening to go with pomp

definitions.meaning: an event or occurrence, something that happens
Elgar's marches are titled Pomp and ___, completing the phrase

explanation.surface: An event accompanied by ceremonial grandeur.
explanation.definitionFit: An occurrence or state of affairs; also the partner of pomp in the set phrase about ceremony.

clue.text: A firing offence

parts.note: firing here is setting fire to things, so the crime is deliberate fire-raising, not one that gets you sacked

explanation.walkthrough: 'firing offence' suggests something that gets you sacked; it is setting fire to property.
explanation.definitionFit: The crime of deliberately setting fire to property, literally an offence of firing.

clue.text: Admirer welcomes one willingly

indicators.note: welcomes means the admirer takes the numeral inside

parts.note: a fan is an admirer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fan gladly greets someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning gladly or with pleasure.

clue.text: Border prepared originally for pot plant

parts.note: a hem is the edge or border of cloth

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of the word prepared

explanation.surface: A border is laid out for a houseplant in a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot plant' looks like a houseplant; pot is cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis, slang name pot, is a variety of this fibre crop.

clue.text: Measure of warmth supplied by a garment of old

parts.note: the tog is the UK unit rating the warmth of duvets and bedding

explanation.surface: A warmth rating is given for an antique piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: TOG ratings appear on British duvets.
explanation.definitionFit: The loose robe worn by citizens of ancient Rome, a garment of long ago.

clue.text: Remove essential parts of tea service after breakage

indicators.note: after breakage says the words tea service are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Clearing away the main pieces of a tea set once it has been smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: To disembowel, or figuratively to strip something of its vital contents.

clue.text: Mysterious character biting top off dried fruit

indicators.note: taking the top off removes the first letter of the fruit's name

parts.note: a prune is a dried plum

explanation.surface: A shadowy figure bites the top off a dried plum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'biting' is link surface; the trim is 'top off'.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet, often seen as magical or secret.

clue.text: Wood alight -— plant recoiling is a brittle thing, consumed

parts.note: a brand is a burning piece of wood

indicators.note: recoiling means the flower's name springs back, read backwards

parts.note: the pansy is a garden flower

explanation.surface: Burning timber, a shrinking plant, something fragile being eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin crisp ginger biscuit, brittle and eaten, hence a brittle thing that gets consumed.
